Restarted on a truly fresh env (note: env.reset() alone did NOT clear ghost/timer state; a new arc.make() env was required), then executed a 3-run plan: ghost A parks on the right car's upper plate (holding the bottom band open), ghost B - padded with 6 no-op delay moves so the runner stays ahead of it - crosses the opened bottom band and parks on the left car's bottom plate (pulling the left car down and opening the goal chamber), and the final run races ahead of ghost B through the one-node choke at (20,50), climbs the left shaft, waits out nothing (timing worked out exactly), and enters the goal ring: levels_completed 2 -> 3, game advanced to level 4. Self-ran the mandatory offline reproduction gate from a fresh reset: reached_level=3, reproduced=True. Stopped after L3: level 4 (glimpsed) adds a horizontal-track car plus two new cage-like ring structures on tracks in a new color - solving it needs its own multi-run discovery plus a longer gate replay, beyond the remaining step budget.
gotchas: env.reset() on an existing offline-arcade env does NOT fully reset g50t: a committed ghost and the depleted action timer survived into the 'fresh' game; create a brand-new env via arc.make() for a genuinely clean instance.
ACTION5 at spawn with an empty trajectory is a free no-op (does not consume one of the 3 run slots).
The 3 run slots are the binding resource: L3 needs BOTH non-final slots spent on plate-holders; any wasted commit makes the instance unwinnable (no un-commit exists short of a full level reset).

Ghosts replay one action per player action and PARK at their endpoint forever; a ghost parked on a corridor node is a permanent wall - choose commit endpoints that are plates, not thoroughfares (my first wasted ghost parked at (44,50) and would have blocked the bottom-band route).

Ghosts replaying the same corridor as your live run WILL share nodes with you; pad the committed trajectory with blocked-direction no-op presses (e.g. 3 at spawn) to control relative timing - 6 pad moves kept the runner safely ahead of ghost B on the shared route.

The x blocker never overlapped/killed the player in ~30 turns of contact-adjacent behavior; it acts as a sliding door, not a hazard, and actually HELPS by vacating the right shaft when approached from the middle shaft.
The per-level action timer (~128 actions) is generous but real; the full 3-run L3 solve used ~71 actions (~36 cells), so heavily exploratory instances should be restarted rather than finished.
The elevator cars snap back the instant their plate is released - there is no transient window; every opened passage needs a permanent holder while you transit.

Multi-line def blocks pasted into the interactive Python REPL silently mangle (NameError/SyntaxError aftermath caused one wasted commit press); use exec-single-string for helper definitions when driving the env interactively.
